scenes.title: The 4 Core Analytical Pillars: BASIC CONCEPTS OF TREND: PEAKS, TROUGHS & SUPPORT/RESISTANCE MECHANICS

beats.hindi_tts: Pillar one: 1. Zigzag Definition of Trend. An uptrend is a series of successively higher peaks and higher troughs; a downtrend requires systematically lower peaks and lower troughs.
beats.en_subtitle: Pillar one: 1. Zigzag Definition of Trend. An uptrend is a series of successively higher peaks and higher troughs; a downtrend requires systematically lower peaks and lower troughs.
beats.en_narration: Pillar one: 1. Zigzag Definition of Trend. An uptrend is a series of successively higher peaks and higher troughs; a downtrend requires systematically lower peaks and lower troughs.

cards.title: 1. Zigzag Definition of Trend
cards.desc: An uptrend is a series of successively higher peaks and higher troughs; a downtrend requires systematically lower peaks and lower troughs.

cards.title: 2. Three Directions of Movement
cards.desc: Markets move up, down, and sideways. Recognizing a trendless horizontal equilibrium prevents devastating trend-following drawdown.

cards.title: 3. Three Hierarchical Degrees
cards.desc: Trends operate across three degrees: Major/Primary (>6 months), Intermediate/Secondary (3 weeks to 3 months), and Near-Term/Minor (<3 weeks).

cards.title: 4. Support & Resistance Mechanics
cards.desc: Support is a price trough where demand overcomes selling pressure; resistance is a peak where supply overcomes buying pressure.

ui_state.question: A stock in an established multi-month uptrend advances to a new high of ₹450, but pulls back sharply to ₹390, dropping below its previous swing reaction low of ₹405. How should a disciplined technician classify the trend status of this stock?
options: A) The uptrend remains 100% intact because the stock hit ₹450 earlier.
B) The uptrend has been formally broken and neutralized; the trend has shifted to sideways or a potential downtrend.
C) The drop below ₹405 is an immediate screaming buy signal.
D) Peaks and troughs have no bearing on trend classification.

ui_state.question: A stock in an established multi-month uptrend advances to a new high of ₹450, but pulls back sharply to ₹390, dropping below its previous swing reaction low of ₹405. How should a disciplined technician classify the trend status of this stock?
options: A) The uptrend remains 100% intact because the stock hit ₹450 earlier.
B) The uptrend has been formally broken and neutralized; the trend has shifted to sideways or a potential downtrend.
C) The drop below ₹405 is an immediate screaming buy signal.
D) Peaks and troughs have no bearing on trend classification.
ui_state.answer: B) Under Murphy's trend definition, an uptrend requires higher peaks and higher troughs. Breaking below a prior trough (₹405 to ₹390) invalidates the uptrend structure.

steps: 1. An uptrend requires successively higher peaks and higher troughs; downtrends require lower peaks and troughs.
2. Markets spend at least one-third of the time in sideways trading ranges: adjust your tools accordingly.
3. Every trend is part of a larger trend degree: always align with the intermediate and primary directions.
4. Support is formed at prior reaction troughs where demand overcomes selling pressure.
5. Resistance is formed at prior reaction peaks where supply overcomes buying pressure.
6. The more times a support or resistance level is tested, the more significant and authoritative it becomes.
7. High volume at a support or resistance level confirms heavy institutional commitment at that price.
8. Never assume a trend has reversed until prices decisively violate the preceding reaction swing pivot.
